author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: One of the best pro-growth tax bills ever has been passed by the Trump administration and the Republicans in Congress. Alongside former President Reagan's 1981 and 1986 tax acts and former President Kennedy's posthumous tax cuts in 1964, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act belongs in the all-time hall of fame. Early lead indicators of the good things to come from the tax-rate cuts are the announcements by Apple, FedEx, AT&T, Fiat Chrysler and over 300 companies of multibillion dollar investments in the United States.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: So disgusted are they that Republican leaders in the White House, Congress and state legislatures have made rigging election rules a top legislative priority, literally ruling out issues and voters they don't like. Consider Missouri (the "Show Me" State): Republicans there showed us what they're made of when they attempted to kill the people's right to amend their state's constitution. In Missouri and 25 other states, a citizen-led initiative process has long allowed people to propose and pass laws of their own instead of always relying on politicians to "do what's right." Yes — it's direct democracy!

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Republicans are supposed to be the party that cuts the job-killing capital gains tax, not the party that raises it. Yet a quirk in the tax bill passed by the Senate could push capital gains taxes higher—and for some long-held assets, the increase may be fairly substantial.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Boys and girls, you probably won't believe that government regulatory officials once saw serving the public as their public duty. Yes, serving the public — get this! And how did they do it? They enforced laws designed to protect consumers, workers, the environment and other targets of raw corporate greed. What a reversal today: the far-right plutocrats behind Trump's Project 2025 have turned our national protection agencies into private escort services for corporate predators.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Taking our attention away from something they've really screwed up and directing it toward something that's not quite so bad — that's the deceptive persuasion Democrats have mastered. Among the chief masters of this technique is the man residing at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave. in Washington, D.C.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Why does the Democratic Socialists of America keep backing Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed to the eyeballs when he keeps calling himself a capitalist? The DSA knows why he has to call himself that: even Democrats in a moderate state like Michigan need to be won over if he is to win. Once he's elected, they firmly expect him to do as they say — which, happily, is in line with what he truly believes.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — The murder of the Kennedy Rose Garden came first, but for the killer in the Oval Office, that was only a prelude. The next likely victim is the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, the arts heartbeat of both the capital and the nation. Lovers of symphony, opera, theater and ballet have been aghast since President Donald J. Trump shut the building in July, stripped the art and declared that, without his name on the wall, it would go bankrupt.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, I explained why I believe Rush Limbaugh was right about Attorney General Eric Holder's resignation: it is by no means a simple bon voyage. Instead, I believe it is a deliberate ploy intended to maneuver Holder into a position of even greater influence, possibly even the Supreme Court.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: But that mission has been twisted backwards by DOJ's present inhabitants. Instead of protecting people seeking justice, the agency is being used to protect corporate abusers from them. Take Big Oil, for example. Despite being a massive polluter, it insists that government authorities must rescue it from its own transgressions. Multibillion-dollar behemoths like Exxon have known for decades that emissions from their fossil fuels are increasing climate change, with intensified fires, floods, etc., causing catastrophic destruction and deaths. Now numerous lawsuits demand that the profiteers behind these horrific losses pay a fair share of the damage they've done.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: President Joe Biden's first joint address to Congress gives us many reasons to reflect on its historical significance. The speech was great, delivered by a man who understands why he holds this role at this time. He knows who we need him to be. And isn't that a relief.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: The Southern Poverty Law Center was likely the largest financial backer of white supremacist groups in the United States—or at least that is what the Department of Justice alleges in its superseding indictment against the SPLC. According to the indictment, the organization secretly paid informants to actively promote and fund racist groups while publicly denouncing and "fighting" those same groups. The SPLC also purportedly created fictitious entities to conceal funding from its donors.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — No, friends, Romans, countrymen, murdering the White House Rose Garden was not enough. Tearing down its stately East Wing, where guests once gathered and mingled, was not enough either. Nor was it enough to brandish "Donald J. Trump" over "John F. Kennedy" on the marble wall of the national performing arts center.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Why do so many grassroots Americans despise today's multibillionaires, those high-tech barons of artificial intelligence (AI)? Their blood-sucking greedhead nature aside, what accounts for it? And by "so many," I mean the hell-raising mass revolt they've sparked: it began in farm country, spread through working-class suburbs and into community colleges and other centers of Middle America, and now includes environmental, religious and democracy movements.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Folks, step right up! There's no need to shove or crowd — we've got plenty for everyone! The Bonanza Extravaganza of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) "BOOM" welcomes you! What Silicon Valley billionaires are proposing now is a scheme that promises an unbelievable windfall to "every citizen." Tech titans such as Sam Altman of OpenAI want the federal government to establish a "public wealth fund," making us commoners investment partners in the construction of the AI wonderworld.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: With fall harvest season comes the familiar sight of pumpkins, cornstalks and perhaps a straw man decorating farm stands and homes. Making a straw man is easy: take a couple of burlap bags, stuff them with hay, then put an old flannel shirt, overalls and a straw hat on your "man." Today's billionaires, corporate elites and other political megadonors, however, have devised a version of their own. Their recipe calls for a couple of silk pillows stuffed with thousand-dollar bills and a finely tailored suit for the fellow. And — viola! — a common straw man becomes a congressman.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Why does Washington's Democratic Party establishment keep demanding that its progressive members tone down their criticism of billionaire oligarchs and corporate autocrats? The insiders want to rebrand the party as ideologically moderate, that's why. "Time to get serious," they bark.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Go ahead and build a ballroom that dwarfs the White House's clean and classic design. Sure, murder the history of Lafayette Square by putting up prison bars that keep tourists away from our traditional place of dissent. And why not close the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts? With your name spoiling the grandeur and the memory of the slain president, it will never be the same again.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: What a glorious June day it was when the Barack Obama Presidential Center opened in Chicago. The opening stood in complete contradiction to the times we've been living through: instead of chaos, community; instead of darkness, lightness; instead of fear, hope.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: You may be asking why President Donald Trump works day after day, in both small and large ways, to destroy faith in democracy. I have an answer, and I will reveal it shortly.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Socialism will always attract an audience because it appeals to base envy and resentment. It is cheap and easy to stir up a mob against "oligarchs," "Wall Street barons," "kulaks," or "billionaires." That is why it was refreshing to hear Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, the fourth richest man on the planet, offer unadulterated praise for the moral and economic superiority of capitalism in his recent interview with CNBC's Andrew Ross Sorkin.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: From Oakland to New York, many across the nation are rallying in protest over the deaths of Michael Brown and Eric Garner. Yet I keep coming back to one question: What about the good cops? We often rush to hang those who are allegedly corrupt, while taking much longer to honor those who honestly serve to protect. The same is true of how we treat our military personnel.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: Cartoonish villains were something writer and philosopher Ayn Rand was often accused of inventing. Consider rogues such as Ellsworth Toohey in "The Fountainhead": driven by a distorted sense of justice, they would scheme to seize the commanding heights of the global economy. Yet people who hold ideas like these exist beyond cartoons and Rand's novels.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: By issuing subpoenas to five pastors, Parker and Feldman initially tried to fly under the radar. The pastors have associations with Christian conservative activists who are rightly suing the city over its claim that they lacked sufficient signatures to place a referendum on the ballot to repeal the equal rights ordinance. In fact, they collected 50,000 signatures when only 17,259 were required.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — After his trip to Turkey, where he went to demand that NATO hand over Greenland!, the Trump whirling dervish has come and gone. Behind him is a city exhausted by his wild Fourth of July displays. But before all that, how great it was to see legions of World Cup soccer fans around the world cheering for their countries at every hour! The England and Mexico teams especially were playing their hearts out. Cape Verde too. Across seams, seas and borders, the pursuit of happiness belonged to everyone, not just us. And Donald Trump hated seeing so many people truly excited.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Once again, Democrats are behaving as though the high moral ground in American politics belongs to them. Yet if 2026 has demonstrated anything, it is this: virtually nothing a left-wing candidate might say or do would draw condemnation from Democrats when that condemnation would threaten their power.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: One of the key lines from President Trump's highly successful speech last week in Davos, Switzerland, was "America is open for business, and we are competitive once again." By going to Davos, of course, Trump was entering the lion's den. Such a visit would have been a poor idea just a year earlier, when elitist heads of state, European Union bureaucrats and international CEOs were uniformly opposed to Donald Trump.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Victory was snatched from the jaws of defeat by the Republican Party when President Trump signed the big tax cut bill. The political and economic landscapes have suddenly changed, with the GOP now having turned the tables on the Democrats.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: Madison, Wisconsin — In my hometown, it's consoling to spend high summer in a sane state. Maine Democrats, meanwhile, fell for the oysterman hook, line and sinker, and what they get in November is what they deserve. They chose Graham Platner, with his rocky record, over Janet Mills, a seasoned woman governor who could have defeated Sen. Susan Collins in a cakewalk. That choice shows we still have a long way to go, baby.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: America, atone. At sundown on Sept. 21, Yom Kippur — the Jewish Day of Atonement and a high holiday — had just passed us by. Thanks to Donald Trump, our country has become the scourge of the world. The clearest demonstration came at the United Nations General Assembly (Tuesday), when Trump asked world leaders whether he should "annihilate" Iran.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: Perhaps a story is where I should begin. My first meeting with Michael J. Fox was in 2006, shortly after Rush Limbaugh mocked the involuntary movements caused by Fox's Parkinson's disease. He had come to Ohio for a rally supporting stem cell research, research that could save countless lives.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Think back to the old-timey days of politics, long, long ago — perhaps 10 years or so? Back in those olden times, a million-dollar donation to a political candidate, whether from someone or from some corporations, would have been scandalous news. A bribe!

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Reigniting economic growth and prosperity is nothing less than what President Donald Trump's pledge to "Make America Great Again" requires. That makes wealth creation essential. Congress is now pivoting to tax reform, a crucial part of creating that wealth. But the president could act on his own by issuing an executive order indexing capital gains for inflation.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: For a moment, put aside the years Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner spent with a Nazi SS Totenkopf tattoo. Put aside, too, his blaming of sexual assault victims for their predicament, his description of rural white Americans as stupid racists and his advocacy of political violence. Then set aside his mockery of a wounded Purple Heart recipient, his joke that the Virgin Mary was a "skank" and his joining a hookup site while married.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: Many of us feel a great deal of excitement, reinforced by repeated waves of relief. We are a nation of survivors. On Inauguration Day, I watched Joe Biden and Kamala Harris take their oaths of office and felt hopeful. They seemed to understand what we were asking of them, and they accepted it without reservation.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Something told me to get to East Potomac Park before Donald Trump destroyed it. So, on a rainy Sunday morning, I went to a rally aimed at protecting the waterfront parkland from his axe. The next weekend, he cut down 430 trees—for a fancy golf course, of course. He began sneakily, on a Saturday morning during the three-day holiday weekend.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Folks, the country is moving down a slippery slope, and we have to stop it before it is too late. Thanksgiving has not even arrived, yet the war on Christmas is already underway. This time, one of the largest public school systems in the United States is removing every reference to religious holidays from its official calendar.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: This past week, my wife, Gena, and I learned what had happened in her small mountain hometown in Plumas County, California: our pastor's church had been kicked out of the county building it rented for Sunday church services. The disgusting part is the political maneuvering engulfing the eviction, aimed at preventing the church from meeting there.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, when Steve Forbes and Art Laffer joined me on my syndicated radio show, I may have taken part in a little piece of radio history. Perhaps never before had these giants of supply-side economics appeared together over the airwaves.

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: "We didn't celebrate the Fourth of July," he told me. "For us, it was the day Vicksburg fell." Vicksburg, Mississippi, fell to Union troops on July 4, 1863. The Confederates surrendered, as was their habit. Long memories continue to mourn the Lost Cause of Black backs whipped bloody.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: As the House and Senate continue working through tax cuts and reform, one point should be clear: both plans are pro-growth, and the main economic force comes from the business side. Where the personal side contributes, the growth will be very limited. That was always the bet.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Campaigning in Iowa on Oct. 27, Vice President Joe Biden said, "Folks, this election is even more important than the two elections you elected Barack and me." He was exactly right. And with President Obama's approval rating having tanked to 38 percent in September, it's understandable to me why Biden is shaking in his boots.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Voter identification laws have the support of a significant majority of Americans. Polls show that Democrats, not just Republicans, believe voters should present ID before taking part in an election. I hear you if you believe our elections need greater security. What I don't buy is the popular contention that failing to pass the SAVE America Act will cost Republicans their congressional majority in the next midterm elections. That's a partisan fantasy fueled by social media.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: For the first time since losing her 2008 presidential campaign, Hillary Clinton returned to Iowa last week. "I'm back," she announced, then went on to say, "It's true. I've been thinking about it," referring to another presidential run in 2016. The truth, however, is that even many among her esteemed liberal cronies consider it a bad idea.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: A truly remarkable promise has come from Washington's Republican policymakers: they've devised a way, they say, to vastly increase America's number of small businesses. Great! Having grown up in a family with a Main Street business in small-town Texas, I take this personally. I know just how hard the little guys have to fight against the raw monopoly power of corporate chains. So I was cheering the GOP ... right up until I discovered that its small business proposal was simply another big business scam.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: The U.S. national debt has just moved past $40 trillion, having doubled in less than a decade. Washington's response has been its familiar fiscal game of blaming the other party. Democrats point to Republican tax cuts; Republicans point to Democratic spending. The reality is that both parties share responsibility, and both rely on the same lie of omission. If we allow it, they will keep steering us into the same wall together.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: On 9/11, we said that we'd "never forget." Yet when our president pursues a no-strategy strategy for stopping Islamic extremists, isn't Washington avoiding both our commitment to remembrance and its responsibility to protect our land and liberties?

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: Back in the 1700s and 1800s, Britain conquered a large part of the world with a navy crewed by unwilling, toothless sailors scarred by the whip and suffering from untreated syphilis. Those are the men you want fighting your wars. Few people fight like men who are mistreated, fed garbage, lashed, and subjected to rape below decks.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Francesca Hong, the Democratic Socialist running for governor of Wisconsin, would be hard to beat for sheer wackiness as a candidate. Defunding the police and abolishing ICE were among her aims, and she topped them off by calling for an end to Thanksgiving. Even "Saturday Night Live" couldn't have invented her.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Between the president's IndyCar auto races, which came and went without a precious Smithsonian artwork being crashed into, and Congress's return, the city takes a deep breath. In the background, cicadas and tennis balls provide the music. Thank god no Cezanne or Renoir was lost while IndyCar drivers circled the National Mall. Some diplomats, meanwhile, were uninvited.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Eric Holder resigned after 5 1/2 turbulent and controversial years as attorney general, during which he was both besieged and bolstered. But is this close friend and confidant of President Barack Obama really stepping down for some benign reason at such a critical moment for the country, or is there a sinister and strategic plan behind the resignation?

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Why was President Donald Trump initially unwilling to share the full text of the framework agreement between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran? There's an obvious first reason: the memorandum of understanding amounts to a capitulation to the regime's clerics.

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: On Sept. 11, 2001, I was working for a medium-sized city newspaper. The Capitol had not yet been stormed, the George Floyd riots had not happened, we had not begun the war in Afghanistan that we were going to lose, and ICE had not killed anyone in the street.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, the right-wing hack, probably does not know what a "petard" is, but he has now been hoisted by a big one. "Hoist on a petard" is a Shakespearean phrase describing a bomb maker being blown sky-high by his own creation.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: When I say the Republican Party has plunged into the abyss of political delirium, that's one thing. Quite another is watching the party confirm its own collective delirium across two entire days of a made-for-TV political talk-a-thon. And the theme? "Bring Back Joe McCarthy!"

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: Here in Washington, D.C., we endure the president's barking, his ever-present red ties and his constant use of capital letters. Each is a form of shouting, part of the psychological warfare he wages as a master of repetition. And now he plans a 250-foot Arch that would obstruct the view from across Arlington Cemetery to the Lincoln Memorial shrine to freedom.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Is being an insufferable jerk something billionaires become, or is it an innate quality they arrive with? Musk, Bezos and Zuckerberg are big-name billionaires who literally flaunt an irrepressible jerkism. But this disease appears to afflict the whole class of uber-rich corporate royals. You won't recognize its telltale symptoms in their grandiose yachts or mansions. Rather, look for the sudden urge to tell us regular people how we ought to think. Now, in particular, they're demanding that we step aside while they remake society in their own image.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Most media pundits and the financial markets are failing to notice the new writing on the wall. Because of several factors, including shrewd moves by President Trump, the odds of significant tax cuts within the next 10 weeks have risen sharply.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: That every citizen lives under the same rules is one of the foundational ideals of a free nation. Democrats are well aware of this; for years, they've lectured us that "no one is above the law."

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Coming up is June 27, the anniversary of the 2024 debate in which America watched Joe Biden tank the election to Donald Trump. Remember? Forgetting would be hard, given the pain Democrats felt as we watched a ghostly Biden self-destruct, struggling to find words. Jill Biden attempted to pretend otherwise. The damage, though, was already done.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: French economist Gabriel Zucman has returned to California with a familiar French answer to a fiscal problem: another tax. Formerly based at the University of California, Berkeley, Zucman is now campaigning for Proposition 40, which would impose an allegedly one-time 5% tax on the net worth of Californians worth more than $1 billion. Zucman, who coauthored the proposition, estimates that the tax could raise about $100 billion and claims that 90% of the proceeds would go to health care.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, "Fox & Friends" featured my latest column, "Neutering Religious Holidays," and liberals quickly came out to defend President Barack Obama's record. That prompted me to do some research: I wanted to see how spiritual Obama's past Thanksgiving addresses had been and compare them with the thoughts of our founding president, George Washington.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Younger Americans often complain that the United States has spent virtually their whole lives bogged down in endless war and interventionism. It's one of their most popular complaints. Well, welcome to history. Whether we like it or not, conflict and meddling have been part of the United States more or less from its inception. War was how the U.S. was born, how it expanded and how it freed its slaves. Through war, it also became a superpower. And until utopia exists, the likelihood that we will need to clash with those threatening our prestige and power remains exceedingly high.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: Inflation is going up, not going away. For the president and Congress, that's a problem with the midterm elections only seven weeks off. Voters hate inflation, but they're not particularly fond of its cure either. That cure has two parts. One is the Federal Reserve's raising of interest rates, as it just did. The other, often overlooked, rests with Congress: unless lawmakers demonstrate that future fiscal surpluses will back the debt, the Fed cannot bring inflation down for good. In other words, Congress must get serious about overspending.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: "The rich are different from you and me." — F. Scott Fitzgerald. Over one weekend, I read two books: Bryan Stevenson's "Just Mercy" on Saturday and Belle Burden's "Strangers" on Sunday. Both are well-told true stories about two countries that exist within America's borders: Death Row in Alabama and Martha's Vineyard in Massachusetts.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Trade protectionism carries this irony: through tariffs and import quotas, we impose on ourselves in peacetime what foreign nations impose on us in wartime through blockades designed to prevent imports from entering our country.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Big Tech, Big Finance and Big Government are colluding to dig us into the unfathomable hole of artificial intelligence, giving that old country saying a newly urgent relevance today. Across the country, entire communities are in an uproar upon learning that their government officials are quietly approving thousands of massive, billionaire-financed data centers. Farmland, local water supplies and each area's electric grid are being usurped. And why? So uber-rich prigs like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos can impose their grandiose, zillion-dollar schemes for displacing us human workers with super-intelligent bots.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: I know this is a generalization. After all, as Mark Twain is said to have said, "All generalizations are false, including this one." Still, evidence is growing that women tend to protect our American democracy more than men do. When partisan schemers attempt to game the electoral system, mostly through rule changes or gerrymandering, women are more willing to put their foot down.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Sometimes I wonder why the billionaire potentates of artificial intelligence have become so despised, and whether they ever wonder about it themselves. Not that it matters. I doubt they do: introspection hardly seems written into the DNA of hubristic AI demigods such as Bezos, Musk and Zuckerberg. And such qualities aren't being programmed into their "superintelligent bots," either.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Q-Anon nuttiness and JD Vance's "Deep State" quackery are examples of wacko right-wing conspiracies that have moved into the center of Republican politics. Their silliness should not hide a different reality: there is, in fact, a very real plot to rig America's political and economic system so that wealth and power move uphill, away from the workaday majority and toward moneyed elites.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: Wrong decade — I beg your pardon. In her mid-40s, Marjorie Taylor Greene clicked "like" on a Facebook post that called for House Speaker Nancy Pelosi to be shot in the head. Comments urging the execution of FBI agents as "deep state" operators seeking to undermine former President Donald Trump also received her likes. And she promoted the conspiracy theory denying that a passenger plane had flown into the Pentagon during the 9/11 attacks.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Roughly 500 days have passed since the IRS was caught red-handed using fear and intimidation to target conservative groups and wage war on them. Among those targeted were tea party patriots, pro-Israel advocates and Christian organizations. Yet here we are, and we the people still haven't seen a single email implicating any IRS official.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: The mayor of Houston first flagrantly violated clergy's First Amendment rights by subpoenaing sermons, and she continues to refuse to rescind her mandate. Now California government officials are forcing churches and other faith-based organizations to fund abortions. What's next?

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: Not long after I began writing a column in the fall of 2002, I started hearing regularly from people who used God as a weapon against LGBTQ rights. That did not surprise me. At the time, I worked at The Plain Dealer in Cleveland and was already very familiar with the bigotry in my home state. Most of the hate mail came from strangers, though blood relatives also gave me their share of lectures. Few things anger right-wing Christians more than a family member insisting that she knows a different version of God.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: President Donald Trump, go ahead and keep the Kennedy Center closed, withholding money for the repairs it needs. For Americans fed up with your extortion schemes, this is low-hanging fruit: there's no need for them to submit to such small-bore intimidation. They can simply shrug off the demand to put your name on the building's facade along with words of gratitude. Or, to switch metaphors, they have bigger fish to fry.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: In 2008, a wave of young supporters and first-time voters ushered Barack Obama into the Oval Office. Now, however, those same voters are among the people most disillusioned with Obama and his regime. They are also the ticket to victory in the 2016 presidential election and to preserving the heart and soul of our republic.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: Are we nearing the point of no return? Please, in a post-Donald Trump world, let America be America again. There is no guarantee that we can rebuild our institutions, arts and trust in government. And if a global economic, environmental or medical crisis arises, that rebuilding endeavor could reach across country boundaries, becoming, as natural historian David Attenborough said, "an international ambition for survival."

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Remember the unhinged cultural revolution we launched a few years ago? Insane, wasn't it — amirite? That, essentially, was what Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) recently told ABC News host Jonathan Karl. She was quoting a New York City Council member whose description concerned past tweets by Francesca Hong, the socialist Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate, about defunding the police and shuttering prisons.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: What a show, huh? This July 4th, big-name corporations pulled out all the stops for a patriotic advertising blitz declaring their devotion to America's democracy. Yet what a Firecracker of Hypocrisy it was! Behind the scenes, many of these showboat patriots have funded the President Donald Trump regime's repression of our people's democratic rights.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Likewise, a small band of partisan lawyers doesn't become a "supreme" court simply because someone calls it one. The six-pack of far-right-wing political activists now proclaiming their own anti-democratic biases as the law of the land have nothing supreme about them; they are soiling our people's ideals of justice. Across economic fairness, women's rights, racial justice, corporate supremacy, environmental protection, theocratic rule and other fundamental issues, these unelected, black-robed extremists are forcing an illegitimate elitist agenda onto America. The people neither want that agenda nor, ultimately, will tolerate it.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Calling Donald Trump merely a bad president doesn't go far enough. Even "King" is too good a word for the likes of him. In the end, what Trump truly is shall be written. Until now, Andrew Johnson was the worst president we've had. Johnson, a Southerner and Abraham Lincoln's vice president, assumed office in 1865 after the Civil War president was murdered by a Confederate sympathizer.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: A public "leader" need not possess every solution. What public leadership requires instead is openness to other people's ideas for solving problems. Franklin Roosevelt demonstrated that strength when he entered the White House amid the full-blown crisis of a national depression. He gathered his top advisers and gave them an open mandate to be creative: "Do something," he told them. "If it works, do more of it. If it doesn't work, do something else."

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: There is an old saying: Those who can, do; those who can't, teach. The debate over wealth taxes in California and elsewhere reflects a similar idea. Those who can, build companies. Those who can't, devise ways for the government to take shares in what other people have built.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Traditional Labor Day images feature men in hard hats and tough women in uniforms—Americans whose muscles were not built in wellness clubs. Photos of the Democratic Socialists of America look very different: they show seas of white, college-educated faces. For most of them, typing is the only work their hands have done. Yet DSA leaders pretend otherwise and promote candidates who play-act as tradespeople.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, Kevin Hassett, President Trump's new chair of the Council of Economic Advisers, delivered his first official speech by walking straight into the lion's den. There, he took the opportunity to pound the leftist Tax Policy Center. What a wonderful sight it was.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: At a recent town hall, Democratic Party's Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed faced repeated demands from Iman Dashti, a Michigan University student, to denounce one of the world's most odious tyrannies. Dashti, who says his family has suffered the Iranian regime's theocratic persecution, confronted El-Sayed over what Dashti described as the candidate's habitual whitewashing and rationalization of Islamic terrorism.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: Evolution at work: in public, a Cheney told the truth. Defying former President Donald Trump's "big lie," as she called it, that the 2020 election victory was stolen, the 54-year-old Wyoming congresswoman took a lonely stand. Her party has no room for truth.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: There was a time, once upon a time, when conservative ideologues stood against government interference in the holy magic of the marketplace. Energy policy provides an example: fossil fuels had right-wing cheerleaders who insisted that government keep its fat thumb off the scale as Big Oil competed in the free market with those frilly new "alternative" sources of energy.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: You know who: Donald Trump, the conqueror whose voice, face and deeds cannot be escaped. On his visit to England, Trump had never heard of William the Conqueror, yet he loved both the word and the idea as applied to his presidency. Delusions of being a Napoleon Bonaparte or Julius Caesar "great man" are his as well.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: Oh good, another war—this time a trade war with Canada, for no obvious reason. Is it meant to give Donald Trump a new stage for big-league bullying? Is it supposed to divert attention from the Jeffrey Epstein files? Who knows. Whatever. Humiliating our closest ally does not serve American interests, ya think?

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: "'I'm dreadin' what I've got to watch,' the Colour-Sergeant said." Those words come from "Danny Deever," a poem Rudyard Kipling wrote in 1890, in India, about a British soldier being hung for murdering a fellow soldier. Kipling was the racist poet of the British Empire who also wrote the made-into-cartoons "Jungle Book."

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: There is apparently at least one point on which most Americans agree. Unfortunately, that point is dangerous: price controls. Remarkable bipartisan support for government price limits appears in a new Wall Street Journal poll. Capping prescription drug prices is supported by 93% of Democrats and 83% of Republicans. Nearly four in five voters favor a 10% cap on credit card interest rates, while large majorities also support caps on child care charges for working families.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: If I had a vote in Congress, it would certainly be a yea for the tax-cut plans the Senate and House have passed, warts and all. Those plans are headed to conference in the coming weeks, where minor differences will be worked out.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: Exchanging money for someone's vote would be hard to surpass as an insulting offer. Yet that is exactly the offer President Donald Trump made: he announced that every adult citizen would receive a $5,000 check if voters kept Republicans in power come the midterms.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Among the wealth of working-class values my parents gave me as I grew up was this nugget of egalitarianism: "Nobody is better than you," they said, "and you're no better than anybody else." From that ethical foundation comes "We're all in this together." Thomas Jefferson enshrined it in the Declaration of Independence; Lincoln consecrated it in his Gettysburg address; and our own pledge of allegiance promises "liberty and justice for all;" The Statue of Liberty welcomes it, Woody Guthrie made it an anthem to the Common Good, and ... well, it's AMERICA!

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Washington, D.C.'s next mayor is likely to be a Marxist. In Los Angeles, Mensheviks and Bolsheviks are fighting for control. New York City, meanwhile, has already fallen to a champion of Third Worldism.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: President Donald Trump has seized the tax cut issue and given it new energy, much as he took back control of U.S. foreign policy in his command performance before the United Nations. Nearly every day, he pounds away at faster economic growth and greater take-home pay, arguing that his plan will make America's economy great again.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Promises of more government checks were probably the inevitable destination of the Right's economic populism as it degenerated. Early in the week, the administration floated a proposal to redirect federal childcare aid, allowing low-income married stay-at-home parents to receive a $9,000 subsidy per child for daycare.

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: Donald Trump, escargot, and gang rape are good examples: all three disgust me, yet some people strongly desire them. Knowing that can make you spend a long time looking around before choosing a seat beside a stranger on the bus. The fact that I can type the word "bus" without instinctively putting "school" in front of it suggests that I may have some history with people whose wants and needs are both disgusting and badly concealed.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Brides should remember that they already have a man. A wedding is not supposed to be a way to attract a date for Saturday night; supposedly, that part is settled for the foreseeable future. That is why it is hard to understand how "naked dressing"—lamentable even in nightclubs—has entered an ancient social custom. Publicly displaying one's privates, or one's underwear, began as a fashion trend promoted by attention-hungry celebrities. Now it is making its way down the aisle.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — This is no Camelot, and Donald Trump is nowhere close to King Arthur. A pretender president, he doesn't even pretend to do right by the people. In all candor, with his fingerprints everywhere, this city of garden squares, memorials and museums feels like a crime scene. The White House East Wing, one of the places we held dear, has been demolished; another, the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, is closed. Yet who can know what's in the knave's heart?

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, Donald Trump stepped back from his earlier proposal for a punitive, across-the-board tariff on imported steel and aluminum. Good decision. Markets rallied because the revised plan targets countries that are cheating and stealing, including China and Russia, while exempting allies.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: Roughly three weeks before Republicans expected an electoral beating, Donald Trump had to remove Kimberly Guilfoyle, his ambassador to Greece. He simply had to. Trump's money-grabbing corruption was wearing thin even among devoted supporters, though the president remained skilled at wrapping his mob-like patter in vague euphemisms and double meanings.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: The purging of many unnecessary federal jobs stands among the most unheralded policy successes of President Donald Trump's second term. Since Jan. 20, 2025, the federal workforce has shrunk by 300,000 jobs to a still-bulky 2.7 million employees. The last time the workforce stood at this level was before President Lyndon Johnson's Great Society vastly expanded the scope of the national government.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: How did this guy get here? From being a TV personality, how did he end up at the head of America's defense department, especially during a war? It was Donald Trump who placed Pete Hegseth in charge of the Department of Defense. Officially, it's now called the War Department, though I'm not ready to go there.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: The higher executives climb toward the top of the corporate ladder, the more IQ they seem to lose. Perhaps that explains the astonishingly stupid policy John Deere's top corporate bosses have imposed on America's farmers. For years, the bosses have decreed that a farmer may "technically owns" a tractor or other John Deere product but, when it breaks down, stalls out, etc., is prohibited from repairing it. Instead, the owner has to call an authorized Deere dealer, even for repairs most farmers could handle themselves.
